sources_read: rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx: Quality Checks row C6 (#5 instruction_leaks_no_grader_machinery) and Internal Quality Checks row 6 (no extra annotation text on this row)
task/tests/scoring.toml, tests/gates/*/{judge.toml,prompt.md}, tests/scored/*/{judge.toml,prompt.md}, tests/app_context.md (for overlap and literal comparison)
.qc-cache/coldwater-strict-2026-10-08-v16-quick and -v15-quick public notes (diff only, to check what changed)
evidence: Agent-visible text = task/instruction.md, the six /instructions notes, /assets/seed_data.json and the agent Dockerfile (copies only instructions/ and assets/). Case-insensitive grep of all of these for judge|rubric|criteri|dimension|reward|weight|score|playwright|claude|glm|/tests|sentinel|gate|probe|verifier|grad|oracle|harbor|mcp|polish|functional|visual|render|constraint returned zero hits. No criterion id (cw_* ids in tests/gates/*/judge.toml and tests/scored/*/judge.toml), dimension name, scoring.toml weight (0.6/0.2/0.2, floor 0.05) or test path appears in public text. Literal comparison: every hyphen/underscore or all-caps token found in tests/** was checked against public text; only ordinary words/contract names overlap (DB_PATH, NODE_PATH, node_modules, case-sensitive, five-second, one-line, read-only, ready-made, two-space) - no probe value or sentinel. Verbatim overlap: longest shared 8+-word run between public text and any judge.toml/prompt.md/app_context.md is 8 words ('selection ends at the very start of the', ui.md line 7 vs scored/functional/judge.toml), which is requirement paraphrase, not rubric leakage. Since the earlier hosted flags: security.md line 3 now names 'localhost or 127.0.0.1' and integration.md line 3 names GET /api/health; these are the public product boundary and the runtime health contract (row 4), not grader sentinels, and security.md does not reveal the probe path. behaviour.md line 13's HTTP line now carries a user reason ('I keep the browser's network panel open'), not a grader rationale; instruction.md's 'check it yourself the way I'll use it' names no verifier. Conforming alternative that could fail: none found under this row. Broken app that could pass: an app that blocks only the literal hostnames localhost/127.0.0.1 from the preview (string match) while leaving other loopback forms reachable could satisfy the stated boundary; that is a security-scope question for rows 25/33, not grader-machinery leakage. Loosening note (outside row 5): v16-quick -> v16-quick2 security.md dropped 'fetch requests to outside addresses ... must fail', so preview egress to external hosts is no longer required to fail; this is a deliberate scope narrowing that row 25 should confirm is matched by the criteria, not a leak.
